To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(a) The subjectivity levels, readability, and spelling errors in reviews matter in influencing sales and the perceived usefulness.

(1) the impact of reviews is affected by multiple text-based features (subjectivity, readability, and spelling errors); (2) the extent of subjectivism in reviews is positively associated with perceived helpfulness, but negatively associated with sales; (3) reviews with a mixture of objective and subjective sentences are more informative (or more helpful) compared to reviews that are only objective or only subjective; (4) reviews that are more readable and have fewer spelling errors are positively associated with product sales and

“the extent of subjectivity in reviews is negatively associated with product popularity, but positively associated with perceived helpfulness of reviews, and that the extent of spelling errors and readability of reviews are negatively associated with perceived helpfuleness of reviews.”
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the information contained in reviews can be mined and analyzed to provide useful insights to manufacturers, consumers, and other interested stakeholders.
understanding and modeling the relationship between the textual and social aspects of online reviews.
the question of how the text of online reviews and characteristics of reviewers influence sales and perceived usefulness of reviews.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the most helpful reviews tend to be those with a mixture of objective information and highly subjective information, and that these reviews are written by reviewers who have a history of writing informative and helpful reviews.
the more objective and informative a review is, the higher its perceived usefulness and the lower its impact on product sales.

the most important features for predicting review impact and usefulness are: the extent of subjectiveness, the readability of a review, the informativeness of a review, and the extent of spelling errors in a review.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the extent of subjective information in reviews is negatively associated with product success, but positively associated with the perceived usefulness of a review.

the quality of a review, as measured by readability, subjectivity, and linguistic correctness, is more important than its quantity, as measured by the number of words in a review or the number of reviews for the product.

we have shown that the extent of review subjectivity, review readability, review informativeness, and reviewer identity disclosure are important factors in determining both the sales impact of the reviews and their perceived usefulness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the text of reviews is an important factor that influences both sales and perceived usefulness of reviews.
a combination of text and reviewer-related characteristics can accurately predict the helpfulness and economic outcomes of online reviews.
the extent of linguistic quality and subjectivity in review text, as well as various reviewer characteristics, are important factors in predicting the economic impact and usefulness of reviews.
